description: Hi! I'm a junior pentester passionate about security, risk scoring, and anomaly detection. I'm launching StarsCare: a visual astronaut health tool linking daily vitals to NASA's 5 Spaceflight Hazards. Join us for a focused plan, strong QA/system design, and fun collaboration! Looking for: frontend/data devs, med/bio enthusiasts, UI/UX designers, and video/pitch storytellers. Beginners welcome!
summary: StarsCare is a web application inspired by mission control, designed to support astronaut health monitoring throughout missions. The platform provides a unified dashboard that integrates an interactive human body map, daily health tracking, real-time risk alerts, and guided self-assessment. Astronauts can log vital signs, sleep patterns, and mood, assess the impact of various spaceflight hazards on different body systems, and monitor their health using a series of color-coded status indicators. The application also offers a range of self-care guidance and enables the generation of concise medical reports in critical situations. A dedicated Flight Surgeon dashboard facilitates remote crew monitoring with appropriate privacy controls and an audited emergency override. StarsCare is intended for deployment across diverse mission environments, including orbital stations, lunar bases, and Mars transits, and features offline data logging and synchronization to address communication delays encountered in deep space. The system emphasizes preventive healthcare, early risk detection, and the promotion of medical autonomy.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

StarsCare is a web-based Mission Control health monitoring and medical triage application built to help astronauts assess their own physical and behavioral health during long-duration space missions—and coordinate safely with Flight Surgeons on Earth.

The platform supports role-based accounts via Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore, offering both Astronaut views (across three mission environments: Orbital Station 0g, Lunar Base 0.16g, and Mars Transit 0g with a 20-minute communication delay) and a Flight Surgeon fleet-monitoring dashboard on Earth:

  • Interactive 2D Body Map: Astronauts can click four anatomical zones (Brain & Behavioral, Heart & Cardiovascular, Immune & Metabolic, and Bones & Muscles) to see live Green/Yellow/Red status, learn how NASA’s 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight affect that system, and read step-by-step, jargon-free instructions on how to take measurements themselves in space.
  • Daily Vitals Check-In & Trend Engine: Crew members log blood pressure, resting heart rate, blood sugar (mg/dL), body temperature, sleep hours, mood, symptoms, and diagnostic image checks. Dynamic 7-day trend charts visualize changes over time while a triage engine evaluates individual thresholds, 7-day personal baseline drift, and compounding multi-system risk (escalating multiple mild Yellow warnings into a Red alert).
  • Live Space Weather Integration: StarsCare queries NASA’s CCMC DONKI API for recent Solar Flares (FLR) and Solar Energetic Particles (SEP), dynamically adjusting the crew’s Space Radiation hazard status (with a cached fallback snapshot for reliability).
  • Gamified Routine & Triage Playbook: Daily checklists (resistive exercise, hydration, dosimeter checks, sleep logs) build a Readiness Score and streak, while Yellow/Red alerts walk the crew through self-care steps or generate a compact, low-bandwidth Flight Surgeon report for Earth.
  • Privacy Mode & Break-Glass Override: Astronauts can keep sensitive mental-health notes locked locally and hidden in Firestore, while the Flight Surgeon has an audited "Break-Glass" emergency override if full access is urgently needed during a medical crisis.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Crew Autonomy Under Delay: Deep-space crews cannot wait 20+ minutes each way for Earth replies during urgent symptoms. StarsCare empowers astronauts to interpret readings and start safe countermeasures immediately onboard.
  • Accessible to Non-Medical Crew: Plain-language measurement guides and color-coded status indicators ensure any crew member can run an assessment without memorizing clinical thresholds.
  • Earlier Detection of Compounding Risks: By tracking 7-day personal baselines alongside live solar radiation alerts and multi-metric rules, StarsCare catches subtle physiological drift before it escalates into an emergency.
  • Higher Honesty in Mental-Health Reporting: Database-enforced privacy protects astronauts from casual exposure or stigma, encouraging consistent behavioral health check-ins while preserving life-saving emergency override capability.
  • Reduced Ground Bandwidth & Alarm Fatigue: Compact telemetry reports summarize critical issues cleanly without flooding limited deep-space communication links, and a calm clinical interface avoids distracting visual clutter.

3. What is the intended impact?

As NASA’s Artemis program and future Mars missions push crews farther from Earth with longer communication delays and higher radiation exposure, medical software must shift from ground-dependent monitoring to crew-centered self-assessment.

StarsCare is designed to improve astronaut safety and daily compliance with preventive health routines (exercise, hydration, sleep hygiene, and radiation sheltering) across lunar bases, orbital stations, and transit spacecraft. Beyond spaceflight, the same offline-first, low-bandwidth triage and audited "Break-Glass" privacy model can translate directly to remote and extreme environments on Earth—such as Antarctic research stations, submarines, maritime crews, and rural telemedicine clinics with limited connectivity.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

  • Frontend & Data Visualization: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts (dynamic 7-day threshold trend charts), Lucide React icons, custom interactive 2D SVG anatomy map, and IBM Plex Sans / IBM Plex Mono telemetry typography.
  • Backend, Authentication & Security: Firebase Authentication (role-based crew & Flight Surgeon demo accounts), Cloud Firestore with persistentLocalCache (offline persistence and real-time sync), custom Firestore Security Rules (least-privilege access & append-only audit logs), and Firebase Analytics.
    • NASA CCMC DONKI API (FLR Solar Flares & SEP Solar Energetic Particles endpoints) for space radiation context.
    • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) — OSD-575 (SpaceX Inspiration4 metabolic, immune, and cardiovascular spaceflight biomarker reference context).
    • NASA Human Research Program (HRP): 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight, The Human Body in Space, and the Human Research Roadmap.
    • NASA OCHMO Technical Briefs & NASA-STD-3001 (Crew Health and Human Factors design principles).

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

  1. Database-Enforced Privacy with an Immutable "Break-Glass" Audit Trail: Rather than merely hiding mental-health notes in the frontend UI, StarsCare enforces isolation inside Firestore Security Rules so private behavioral logs cannot be queried by anyone else—including the Flight Surgeon—until an emergency override is triggered. Activating "Break-Glass" requires a documented clinical justification and writes a permanent, non-deletable record (allow update, delete: if false) to an Audit Log visible to both the Flight Surgeon and the astronaut.
  2. Real-Time Space Weather + Multi-Metric Triage: Instead of treating human vitals in isolation, StarsCare blends personal 7-day physiological drift with live NASA CCMC DONKI solar flare/SEP alerts and mission-specific hazard profiles (0g vs. 0.16g vs. Mars delay).
  3. Deep-Space Signal Blackout Simulation & Low-Bandwidth Reporting: Built-in offline queueing demonstrates how astronauts continue logging and receiving local triage guidance during communication blackouts, automatically syncing when signal returns and packaging alerts into minimal-text packets for Ground Control.

6. What factors did the team consider?

  • Human Factors & Stress Usability (NASA-STD-3001): Under high stress or fatigue, cluttered screens cause errors. We chose a high-contrast, matte dark-mode clinical layout with tabular monospace numbers, strict Green/Yellow/Red color meaning, and plain-English instructions so astronauts never have to guess what a number means.
  • Communication Latency & Connectivity (Distance from Earth): Knowing Mars missions face long one-way delays and orbital blackouts, we designed local-first triage calculations, Firestore offline caching, and compact Ground Control summaries.
  • Privacy, Stigma & Clinical Safety (Isolation & Confinement): We balanced astronauts' reluctance to share sensitive behavioral notes (via PIN-masked UI and locked Firestore subcollections) against the life-safety need for Flight Surgeons to access full records if a crew member becomes incapacitated (via audited Break-Glass overrides).
  • Data Grounding & Demo Reliability: To ensure external API rate limits or network drops never interrupt evaluation, live NASA CCMC DONKI queries are paired with transparent cached fallback indicators, OSDR (OSD-575) reference context, and one-click pre-seeded demo accounts so judges can test both Astronaut and Flight Surgeon workflows immediately.
